input.summary: Full ledger built and traced; no findings. (1) Claims: every limitation of independent claims 1, 11 and 16 and of dependent claims 2-10, 12-15 and 17-20 was traced to an affirmative disclosure passage — rigid base with first/second side, motor coupled to the first side, air-extraction mechanism coupled to the first side and in fluid communication with a chamber on the second side ("An air-extraction mechanism, such as a vacuum pump, is also coupled to the first side and is in fluid communication with a chamber located on a second side of the base"); rigid low-friction perimeter member at the perimeter of the second side ("The perimeter of the second side is formed as a rigid loop or skirt made from a low-friction material such as plastic, metal, PTFE, or a combination of rigid materials"); no complete airtight seal, restricted-but-open airflow and the clearance ("is not intended to form a complete airtight seal ... restricts airflow into the chamber while maintaining rigid contact with the tile ... continuously removes air entering beneath the rigid perimeter"); sub-atmospheric chamber and holding force without operator downforce ("maintaining the chamber at a lower pressure than the surrounding atmosphere. The resulting pressure differential holds the device firmly against the tile without requiring the operator to press downward"); all-rigid vibration path free of rubber/foam ("connected to the tile through rigid components ... does not rely on flexible rubber or foam"); sliding while held ("the low-friction perimeter allows the device to slide freely across different areas of the tile while the vacuum continuously maintains contact"); handle for guiding; rope/wire/cable pulling element and decoupled control; PTFE and material lists; vacuum pump; continuous running. Claim 10 and the autonomous-mode text trace to the sole substantive USER passage in conversation.md ("we can add small stirring elements and let the vibrations cause a constant forward motion" ... "we don't even need to pull or move it with the hand"); the remaining USER turns are operational resume/repair instructions and were treated as non-disclosure. (2) Numerals: all seventeen entries (10, 12, 14, 16, 18, 20, 22, 24, 26, 34, 36, 38, 40, 42, 44, 46, 48) carry one meaning across the numeral table, the detailed description and every brief; each appears on at least one sheet and every figure's numeral list matches its identification entries exactly (FIG. 1: 10/12/18/20/24/36/44; FIG. 2: 12/14/20/22/24/36; FIG. 3: 16/24; FIG. 4: 24/26/34/36/38/40/42; FIG. 5: 10/36/46; FIG. 6: 10/48). (3) Figures: all six briefs were checked against the Brief Description of the Drawings; the section designations repeat identically in the source view, the resulting view and the drawing description (FIG. 3 horizontal line labelled 2 at both ends -> FIG. 2 "taken on line 2-2 of FIG. 3" -> 07-drawings; FIG. 3 vertical line labelled 4 at both ends -> FIG. 4 "taken on line 4-4 of FIG. 3" -> 07-drawings). FIG. 2 showing the perimeter member bearing on the covering element and FIG. 4 showing the clearance at a place where it is present are mutually consistent with the "along at least part of the perimeter member" recitals in the claims and description. Depiction choices with no disclosed appearance — the rectangular slab/ring/block outlines, band depth, block order and spacing, the flat lower end of the perimeter member, the schematic passage giving fluid communication between the housing and the chamber, the attachment of the cord, and the number and carriage of the stirring elements — are each expressly confined to the figure briefs as conventions and disclaim form, position, contact and construction; none of them verbalizes a taper, angle, runout, depth-asymmetry, port construction or contact topology beyond what the disclosure affirmatively states, and no functional-surface geometry statement was found that lacks source support. (4) Application text: the title, "Not applicable." cross-reference and government-support sections match input/brief.md; the Field, Summary, Detailed Description and Abstract use the same relationships and terminology as the claims; the Brief Description states only "shown schematically", "shown in section/elevation" and "omitted for clarity" and nowhere adds an "by way of example" outline, an "any closed outline" statement or any other embodiment introduced to justify a renderer's choice; no drafting note, placeholder, open question, instruction to a person, unresolved alternative or internal comment remains in any section body, and no section heading is duplicated inside a body. Background prior-art characterizations with [REF:...] markers were left to the separate citation review and no invention matter rests on them.

content.text:
I reviewed every input file, all ten draft sections, the numeral ledger, and all six figure briefs, and built the full source ledger before answering.

**What I traced**

- **Claims 1–20:** every limitation maps to the disclosure — rigid base with first/second sides, motor on the first side, air-extraction mechanism on the first side in fluid communication with a second-side chamber, rigid low-friction perimeter loop (plastic/metal/PTFE/combination), deliberate non-seal with continuous ambient inflow, sub-atmospheric chamber, holding without operator downward force, all-rigid transmission path, low-friction sliding without releasing the hold, guiding handle, rope/wire/cable pulling element with decoupled control. Claim 10 (stirring elements causing constant forward motion) traces to the single technical USER turn: *"we can add small stirring elements and let the vibrations cause a constant forward motion."*
- **Numerals 10–48:** each has one meaning across description, claims, briefs and the ledger; each appears in at least one brief; every numeral named in a brief is in the ledger.
- **Figure briefs vs. Brief Description:** the parts enumerated in `draft/07-drawings.md` correspond exactly, figure by figure, to the numerals in each brief (including the FIG. 2 sectioned-bodies wording). Section designations 2-2 and 4-4 are used identically in FIG. 3 (source view), FIG. 2/FIG. 4 (resulting views), and the drawing description.
- **Depiction conventions:** the schematic slab/band/blocks, the rectangular plan form, the flat bearing-face end, the FIG. 2 communication gap, the pulling-element attachment and the stirring-element blocks are all disclaimed inside their briefs only. No "by way of example", "any closed outline", or renderer-justifying embodiment leaks into the application text, and the briefs verbalize no undisclosed depth, taper, angle, runout or contact-topology relationship for the bearing face, clearance or port.
- **Formalities:** title, applicant/inventor, and the two "Not applicable." statements match `input/brief.md`; no drafting note, placeholder, question, instruction or unresolved alternative remains in any section; the abstract is 148 words.

The operational "resume/repair/publish" USER turns were treated as context only, not as disclosure.

I found no untraced technical assertion and no verified internal inconsistency, so the findings array is empty.

input.summary: Full ledger built and closed with no unsupported matter. All 20 claims were traced limitation by limitation to affirmative inventor passages: rigid base with first and second sides, vibration motor coupled to the first side, air-extraction mechanism (vacuum pump) coupled to the first side and in fluid communication with a second-side chamber, rigid loop/skirt perimeter of plastic, metal, PTFE or a combination of rigid materials, deliberate absence of a complete airtight seal with continuous ambient inflow beneath the rigid perimeter, extraction sufficient to hold the chamber below atmospheric pressure, holding force supplied by the pressure differential rather than the operator, all-rigid low-damping transmission path free of rubber/elastomer/foam, low-friction sliding to successive areas without releasing the hold, guiding handles, and a rope/wire/cable flexible pulling element giving decoupled position-versus-hold control. Claim 10, the Summary's autonomous paragraph, the Field's "autonomously moving" clause, the FIG. 6 brief and the corresponding detailed-description paragraph all trace to the single technical USER turn adding stirring elements and vibration-driven constant forward motion; the operational resume/repair/publish turns were treated as context only. Every numeral 10, 12, 14, 16, 18, 20, 22, 24, 26, 34, 36, 38, 40, 42, 44, 46 and 48 was checked for a single consistent meaning across the numeral table, the description, the claims and all six figure briefs, and each appears in at least one brief with its brief list matching its numeral header. All six figure briefs and the Brief Description of the Drawings were compared part by part and agree exactly, including the sectioned bodies of FIG. 2, the omitted motor and handle, and the omitted motor and pump in FIG. 5; section designations 2-2 and 4-4 carry the same repeated designation in the FIG. 3 source view, in the FIG. 2 and FIG. 4 resulting views and in the drawing description. Schematic choices (rectangular slab, band, blocks, ring plan form, flat bearing-face end, the FIG. 2 communication gap, the pulling-element meeting, the stirring-element blocks) are disclaimed inside their briefs only, add no undisclosed depth, taper, angle, runout, port construction or contact topology, and no "by way of example" or "any closed outline" broadening reaches the application text. Background prior-art characterizations were left for the later citation trace. Title, applicant, inventor and both "Not applicable." statements match the brief; no drafting note, placeholder, question, instruction, unresolved alternative or internal comment remains, and the abstract is 148 words. No untraced technical assertion and no verified internal inconsistency was found.
